> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19bac1cbdbf823661979e4c3c79ddef496ff92a3` — the merge of head `564aa992b5f44df41ab4b350fc08934b40516d24` into base `a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19bac1cbdbf823661979e4c3c79ddef496ff92a3 && git checkout 19bac1cbdbf823661979e4c3c79ddef496ff92a3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30 564aa992b5f44df41ab4b350fc08934b40516d24 && git checkout -B drift-repro a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30 && git merge --no-ff 564aa992b5f44df41ab4b350fc08934b40516d24

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31952 (Fixes #31901) · 2026-11-09T16:10Z

Head-sha: `564aa992`

- **Form:** draft to `main` under `Fixes #31901`. `Clause-②: no`: the indexes come out the same, and only PostgreSQL's way of building them changes. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Patch changeset.
- **Premise on `main` `2b880f12` (`31901-step0.md`, PG 16.15, 1M rows):** today an existing-table `CREATE INDEX` blocks a concurrent INSERT for 537–777 ms. With `CONCURRENTLY` the wait is 1.2–1.3 ms.
- **Change, as ruled (A, then ①C):**
  - On an existing PG table, the backfill runs `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` on its own autocommit session. This covers boot sync, `os migrate` apply and existing rotation shards.
  - A unique index runs `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates` before any DDL. If duplicates exist, no DDL is sent and the existing durability log is written.
  - `getExistingIndexNames` reads `indisvalid`, and a managed INVALID index is dropped `CONCURRENTLY` and rebuilt.
  - The PG wait is bounded by `lock_timeout` at the existing 120 s, with `55P03` recognised and PG wording on the refusal.
  - After the first timeout a 120 s window opens (`ConcurrentIndexDeferral`). Inside it, other builds defer without waiting; when it expires it closes itself, so a process waits at most once per 120 s. `flushDeferredSchemaDdl` and the public `applyMigrationEntries` clear the window on entry.
  - A plain unique constraint is attached `USING INDEX`.
  - New tables and the other dialects get byte-identical DDL.
- **Deviation accepted:** the boot's own `reconcileAndWarnDrift` (autoMigrate `safe`) calls `applyMigrationEntriesKeepingDeferral`, which leaves the window in place. Clearing it on every object would bring back one 120 s wait per object, which is the thing the guard prevents. The public entry still clears unconditionally. This is pinned and ablated.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION, confirmed by this ACCEPT:** `.changeset/31882-implicit-reference-index.md` is pending on `main` (#31882, this seat's card) and goes out in the same release. Its sentence "On PostgreSQL the build is a plain `CREATE INDEX`, which blocks writes to that table while it runs" would be false once this PR lands. It now reads "On PostgreSQL an existing table builds them with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, so writes to the table are not blocked while they build; see this release's entry on concurrent index backfills…". The Check Changeset red on this head is that refusal, by design. Restoring the old note would put the false sentence back. The seat added the file through claim amendment 6742380548.
- **Pins and ablations:** 11/11 live on PG 16 (with MySQL 8 in the CONTROLs):
  - a write during the build is not blocked;
  - an INVALID index is cleaned up and rebuilt, and the next sync does nothing;
  - a lock-wait timeout defers instead of hanging;
  - one wait per window, and the next sync after expiry rebuilds;
  - the public `applyMigrationEntries` does not inherit the window;
  - the boot reconcile keeps it.
  Six ablations, each red, then restored clean.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31952` reports NOT governed, +951/−36. K = 2 first-parent commits on `main` since the merge base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 71, all exit 0 except the by-design changeset red. driver-sql: 4205 passed; the 17 live index files: 343/343. Typecheck and eslint exit 0. CI on this head: Test Core 8/8, Type Check and Lint & Repo Gates green. Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) was skipped by path, so the live evidence is the dev's local PG 16.15 and MySQL 8.0 run.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31901, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closes through `Fixes`.
